Rescuers have finished removing victims from a damaged commuter train car after a crash outside Indonesia’s capital killed 15 people, all of whom were women.

The death toll was confirmed Tuesday after rescue crews completed their search for trapped victims.

The women died when a long-distance train collided with a stationary commuter service outside Jakarta on Monday. The collision occurred at Bekasi Timur Station when a long-distance train struck the rear of the stopped commuter service.

The victims were inside a car designated for women only, a common accommodation to stop harassment.

In addition to the deceased, 88 people were taken to hospitals for treatment, according to Bobby Rasyidin, CEO of state-owned railway company PT Kereta Api Indonesia. The bodies of those killed have been transported to a hospital for identification.

open image in gallery Passengers are seen being rescued after the train crash in Bekasi, Indonesia ( AP )

Mr Rasyidin stated: "We are currently ensuring that all victims receive the best possible care."

Rescue teams concluded the evacuation of all victims from the wreckage by mid-morning on Tuesday. Mohammad Syafii, head of the National Search and Rescue Agency, confirmed: "There are no further casualties."

All 240 passengers aboard the Argo Bromo Anggrek long-distance train were reported safe.

Police have launched an investigation into the cause of the accident, with Jakarta Police Chief Asep Edi Suheri addressing reporters at the scene.

The Indonesian Ministry of Transportation indicated in a written statement that authorities believe the incident began when another commuter train hit a stalled taxi near Bekasi Timur Station.

open image in gallery Workers and rescuers examine the wreckage following the collision ( AP )

This initial event reportedly led to the second commuter train stopping at the station, where it was subsequently struck by the long-distance service.

Mr Rasyidin added: "As for the chronology of events, we are leaving it to the National Transportation Safety Committee to investigate the cause of tonight’s train accident in greater detail."

The incident highlights ongoing concerns about Indonesia’s aging railroad network, which has a history of accidents.

In January 2024, a separate collision between two trains in West Java province resulted in at least four deaths.

News.title: The iPhone Ultra is Apple’s first folding phone, here’s what we know
News.content:
Rumoured for years, 2026 could finally be the year Apple launches its first folding phone. Predicted to be called the iPhone Ultra, it would be the first major product launch under new chief executive John Ternus as Apple looks to take on the likes of Samsung and Google.

It’s just the first of several products set to define Apple’s Ternus era. The iPhone Ultra is expected to take on a book-style design that opens out into a tablet-like display. The tech giant will apparently bring a completely crease-free design, with the latest mock-ups showing what the iPhone Ultra could look like in September.

September won’t just be the start for Ternus, but also a strategy shift for Apple itself. The company will reportedly punt the regular iPhone 18 to spring 2027 for the first time, with Apple reserving its September keynote purely for the iPhone Ultra and the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Here’s everything I know so far about the upcoming foldable, from price and release date to design, camera and specs.

Latest Apple iPhone Fold rumours

While there have been plenty of rumours about the name of Apple’s folding phone, a new report from Macworld claims it may be called the iPhone Ultra. On 27 April, the publication said the device would be only the second to carry the Ultra branding, after the high-end Apple Watch Ultra. Apple could then expand the name to other devices, with a touchscreen MacBook Ultra tipped for next year, alongside a possible iPad Ultra.

On 22 April, Vadim Yuryev from the Max Tech YouTube channel shared a series of images and videos of dummy units of Apple’s rumoured foldable iPhone. What’s immediately clear is that Apple might not be going tall with its first foldable like Samsung and Google, but opting for something wider and more compact instead, fitting more easily inside a pocket.

When comparing the iPhone Fold to the iPhone 17 Pro Max in its unfolded state, it appears the foldable is roughly the same width as the Pro Max in landscape but significantly taller. That could make it way better for watching content on the go with a 4:3 aspect ratio.

It looks absolutely tiny when closed. According to previous leaks, the iPhone Fold could boast similar dimensions to an iPhone 13 mini when shut, with a 5.5in outer display. Yuryev also demonstrated how easy it is to reach across the screen in its folded state, showing it can be used one-handed. You can also see the power button on the right, predicted to house a Touch ID sensor, as well as the camera control button. Similar to an iPad mini, the volume buttons can be seen on the top edge.

Yuryev also compared the iPhone Fold dummy to an 8.3in iPad mini. Barring the mini’s thick bezels, they look roughly the same size, so it could be like having an iPad mini in your pocket. Interestingly, Yuryev’s dummy is 11mm thick, which is different to previous rumours that suggested it could be 9mm thick when closed.

I’ve rounded up every iPhone Fold rumour below.

Apple iPhone Fold release date

Apple has reportedly been working on a foldable smartphone for years. In January 2021, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that the tech giant had begun early work on a foldable iPhone and was already testing prototype foldable displays internally.

We’ve been waiting for it to launch ever since. In 2021, Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo speculated the folding iPhone could launch as early as 2024. Evidently, that never happened. Due to the challenges in manufacturing a foldable iPhone without a crease, there have been delays, leading Kuo to suggest last year that it would launch in 2026 instead.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman gave us a better idea of this potential launch strategy in late 2025. He stated that Apple would move towards a more spread-out launch window from September 2026, only launching the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max here, as well as the all-new iPhone Fold.

But in March 2026, Barclays analyst Tim Long claimed in a research note that, while the iPhone Fold will launch alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max in September, it won’t be released until December. Apple has used this strategy in the past, delaying the iPhone X launch until December but keeping the iPhone 8 release in September.

While a report from Nikkei Asia claimed in early April that Apple had faced setbacks during the engineering test phase for the iPhone Fold, potentially delaying the phone even further into 2027, Gurman said on April 7 that it was still on track to launch this September.

Whenever it actually releases, it looks very likely that the iPhone Fold will at least be announced this September, even if shipments could slip to December. I’m expecting the Apple event to take place on Tuesday, 8 September or Wednesday, 9 September, where it’ll unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, alongside the new folding iPhone.

Apple iPhone Fold price

It’s difficult to predict the price of an all-new smartphone, but there are a lot of rumours floating around, and it might not be a great sign for your wallet – the iPhone Fold could be the most expensive iPhone ever.

In early April, Gurman claimed the iPhone Fold could cost more than $2,000 (£1,500). He said that could deter many customers, but should boost the company’s average sales price. In March 2025, Ming Chi-Kuo also speculated that the iPhone Fold could cost between $2,000 and $2,500 (£1,850)

Weibo leaker Instant Digital shared the potential storage options and prices for each one in March 2026. According to the insider, the three prices for the different storage options are as follows:

256GB: $2,320 (£1,720)

$2,320 (£1,720) 512GB: $2,610 (£1,940)

$2,610 (£1,940) 1TB: $2,900 (£2,150)

While often correct about many things, pricing is the most difficult thing to predict when it comes to anything Apple. Annual price hikes have always been predicted for the regular iPhone range, and more often than not, they don’t come to fruition, so take those ballpark prices with a pinch of salt.

Apple iPhone Fold design and display

As mentioned previously, Apple has been tinkering with various folding designs for a while now. One of the options was a clamshell-style folding phone. Like the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip line, but according to Ming-Chi Kuo, the tech giant decided on a book-style design, similar to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold, meaning it’ll open out into a larger tablet when unfolded.

In March last year, Kuo claimed the foldable iPhone would boast a 7.8in crease-free inner display and a 5.5in outer display. That’s interesting because if Apple goes for a 5.5in display, the cover screen will be much smaller than rival foldables.

Kuo also said that it’ll have a crease-free design, a difficult feat that no mainstream phone manufacturer has quite achieved yet. The insider also stated that the hinge will combine stainless steel and titanium alloy, while the casing will use titanium alloy only.

In terms of thickness, Kuo claims it will be between 9 and 9.5mm when folded shut, and 4.5 to 4.8mm thick when unfolded like a tablet. It will, however, only have two cameras on the rear and two front-facing cameras that can be used when folded or unfolded. There reportedly won’t be any room for Face ID, however, with Apple expected to use a Touch ID side button.

In December 2025, The Information leaked more details about the iPhone Fold’s dimensions. According to the outlet, it has a 5.3in display when folded, expanding to 7.7in when unfolded. What’s most intriguing is the aspect ratio, with hints that it’ll be wider than tall. The publication claims it’ll have a 2:3 aspect ratio, expanding to 4:3 when unfolded.

In March 2026, Apple Track created a realistic-looking concept of what the iPhone Fold might look like based on the latest design leaks. The YouTube channel stated that each display will have its own Dynamic Island.

In early April 2026, insider Sonny Dickson leaked dummy pictures of what the iPhone Fold will reportedly look like when it launches in September.

On 16 April, reliable leaker Majin Bu showed off images of what it claimed were the final designs of the iPhone Fold. It shows an almost-square display, with a camera bar that looks similar to the iPhone Air. On 19 April, Bu also leaked the cases, indicating that it will feature MagSafe, so you can charge your phone wirelessly and attach magnetic accessories.

According to Korean publication The Elec, the iPhone Fold will boast two OLED displays that use Samsung Display’s CoE (Color filter on Encapsulation) technology, which has been used on the Galaxy Z Fold series since 2021, which should make the displays more efficient and thinner.

Apple iPhone Fold cameras

There isn’t a huge amount of detail about the cameras just yet, but Ming Chi-Kuo stated in 2025 that it will feature a dual lens setup, rather than a triple lens rear.

In June 2025, Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claimed the dual camera rear setup will feature 48MP, matching the iPhone 17 Pro’s main cameras.

According to a JP Morgan industry report, seen by MacRumors, the iPhone Fold’s outer display (when folded) will feature a 24MP under-screen camera built into the inside display. This would be huge if true, given that many under-display sensors are notoriously bad in terms of picture quality.

iPhone Fold specs and battery life

There’s even less information about the iPhone Fold’s specs. According to analyst Jeff Pu, the iPhone Fold will boast Apple’s A20 chip, built on TSMC's 2nm process. It will reportedly be 15 per cent faster and 30 per cent more efficient than the A19.

In March 2026, Korean outlet The Bell claimed the iPhone Fold will feature 12GB of RAM, something supplied by Samsung

Battery life is expected to be absolutely mammoth, however. A post from a leaker on the Korean Naver blog claimed in November 2025 that it will boast a huge 5,400 to 5,800mAh battery – the biggest capacity of any iPhone ever.

Best iPhone 17 Pro contract deals

iPhone 17 Pro with 100GB data Affordable Mobiles currently has one of the cheapest iPhone 17 Pro deals. You can get the phone with 100GB of data for £53 per month and a £39 up-front cost. The deal is with mobile network Three, meaning you get access to Three+ rewards and free wifi on the London underground. £53 from Affordablemobile.co.uk Prices may vary

iPhone 17 Pro Max with 25GB of data Tesco Mobile currently has one of the best iPhone 17 Pro Max deals right now. Clubcard members can get the iPhone 17 Pro Max with 25GB of data for £49.99 per month, down from £55.99 per month. That’ll save you £216 over the course of your contract. Tesco Mobile piggybacks off O2’s network, so you’ll still get the same speeds as if you were with O2 direct. £50 from Tescomobile.co.uk Prices may vary

The FTSE 100 nudged higher on Tuesday as investors weighed the Middle East crisis and reports that OpenAI has missed internal targets for users and revenue.

The FTSE 100 closed up 11.70 points, 0.1%, at 10,332.79. The FTSE 250 ended down 180.01 points, 0.8%, at 22,399.42, and the AIM All-Share fell 8.28 points, 1.0%, at 786.90.

Oil prices climbed once more with Qatar warning of the possibility of a “frozen conflict” in the Gulf, as talks between the US and Iran for a peace deal appeared to be at a stalemate.

Brent oil traded at 111.77 US dollars a barrel on Tuesday afternoon, higher compared to 108.92 dollars at the time of the equities close in London on Monday.

Aside from the Iran war, analysts reacted to news that the United Arab Emirates is quitting the Opec and Opec+ groups of major oil-producing nations next month after nearly 60 years of membership.

The UAE said its decision would help it meet growing global energy demand in the long-term after recent investments to boost its production capacity.

Michael Brown at Pepperstone said the main surprise is in “its timing, as opposed to its substance”.

While this is undoubtedly a “pivotal” event for the global energy market, Mr Brown said, the near-term implications of the move are likely to be “relatively limited”.

“Though the UAE have pledged to ‘gradually’ increase production after their departure, it goes without saying that actually doing so at present is somewhere between difficult, and impossible.

“As the US-Iran conflict continues, and the Strait of Hormuz remains impassable, the most significant issue for the crude market is not production, but actually shipping product to where it is needed. Today’s announcement does not change anything on that front,” he said.

Mr Brown noted the UAE’s dissatisfaction with Opec has been “clear for some time, with the country of the belief that Opec quotas are an unfair limit, constraining the nation’s major infrastructure investment projects”.

Saul Kavonic, head of energy research at MST Financial, told the BBC it was “the beginning of the end of Opec”.

“With the UAE leaving, Opec loses about 15% of its capacity and one of its most compliant members,” Mr Kavonic said.

In European equities on Tuesday, the CAC 40 in Paris ended down 0.5%, and DAX 40 in Frankfurt fell 0.3%.

In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.2%, the S&P 500 was 0.8% lower, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 1.4%.

Tech stocks bore the brunt of Tuesday’s falls in the US, after a Wall Street Journal (WSJ) report said OpenAI had missed internal targets for users and revenue, stoking fresh fears about whether massive spending on AI infrastructure can be sustained.

The WSJ said that OpenAI had missed its own goal of reaching one billion weekly active users for ChatGPT by the end of 2025 and fell short of multiple monthly revenue targets this year.

According to the report, OpenAI chief financial officer Sarah Friar has privately warned company leaders that the firm might be unable to meet future computing contract obligations if revenue growth does not accelerate.

Oracle fell 3.6%, Advanced Micro Devices by 3.5%, and Nvidia by 2.1% as the report caused a ripple effect across technology stocks.

But Wedbush Securities pushed back against the report.

“Overall, we believe OpenAI has been tracking very high demand on both the consumer and enterprise front and we strongly disagree with the notion that growth is weakening. We would be buyers of AI-driven tech stocks this morning and in particular Oracle on this way overreaction to this WSJ report in our view,” the broker said.

The yield on the US 10-year Treasury was 4.36% on Tuesday, widening from 4.32% on Monday. The yield on the US 30-year Treasury stretched to 4.96% from 4.93%.

The pound eased to 1.3505 US dollars on Tuesday afternoon from 1.3549 dollars on Monday. Against the euro, sterling ebbed to 1.1534 euros from 1.1543 euros.

The euro traded lower against the US dollar, falling to 1.1709 dollars on Tuesday from 1.1733 dollars on Monday. Against the yen, the dollar was trading at 159.61 yen, higher from 159.27 yen.

On the FTSE 100, BP rose 1.1% after better-than-expected first-quarter results, which benefited from the surge in oil prices.

The London-based oil major said underlying replacement cost profit ballooned to 3.20 billion dollars in the first quarter of 2026 from 1.38 billion dollars the year prior, well ahead of 2.67 billion dollars expected by the company-compiled market consensus.

Barclays eased 0.2% as in-line results failed to energise its share price.

The London-based lender said pre-tax profit rose 3.3% to £2.81 billion in the first quarter of 2026 from £2.72 billion a year before, just shy of the company-compiled consensus of £2.83 billion.

Jefferies analyst Jonathan Pierce said the results were “solid enough” with “no fireworks”.

A weaker gold price hit Fresnillo, down 2.0%, and Endeavour Mining, down 4.5%. The yellow metal traded down at 4,579.32 dollars an ounce on Tuesday, from 4,677.74 dollars at the same time on Monday.

On the FTSE 250, Telecom Plus tumbled 17% as it guided to low-end full-year profit, while SSP fell 5.5% as UBS downgraded to “neutral” from “buy”, noting risks to volumes in the travel retail industry linked to the Middle East conflict are increasing.

Elsewhere, building materials firm Travis Perkins and house builder Taylor Wimpey slid 4.0% and 5.3%, respectively, as investors weighed trading updates.

The biggest risers on the FTSE 100 were DCC, up 145.00p at 5,380.00p, Airtel Africa, up 8.20p at 355.40p, Centrica, up 4.10p at 211.20p, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, up 135.00p at 7,260.00p, and British American Tobacco, up 76.00p at 4,312.00p.

The biggest fallers on the FTSE 100 were Endeavour Mining, down 195.00p at 4,191.00p, Antofagasta, down 122.00p at 3,488.00p, Anglo American, down 111.50p at 3,520.00p, Compass Group, down 0.80p at 28.52p and Experian, down 74.00p at 2,824.00p.

Wednesday’s global economic calendar has interest rate decisions in the US and Canada, German inflation data and US durable goods figures.

Wednesday’s local corporate calendar has first-quarter results from pharmaceutical firms AstraZeneca and GSK, lender Lloyds Banking Group and consumer products firm Haleon.

Rising Spanish star Rafael Jodar continued his dream Madrid Open debut by setting up a blockbuster quarter-final with world No 1 Jannik Sinner.

The 19-year-old is attempting to fill the void left by the injured Carlos Alcaraz and defeated Vit Kopriva 7-5 6-0 to reach his first Masters quarter-final.

Jodar’s stunning rise has seen the Madrid local win 12 of his last 13 matches on clay, including a title in Marrakech and a run to the Barcelona semi-finals last week.

He was still ranked outside of the world’s top 200 in November but the teenager is now set to be seeded for the French Open and potentially inside the world’s top 30 by Monday.

Before then, he must attempt to end Sinner’s 20-match win streak at Masters events after the Italian defeated Britain’s Cameron Norrie earlier on Tuesday.

Jodar’s match against Kopriva was given top billing in Madrid, with Sinner moved to a morning slot to accommodate him, and they will take centre stage on Wednesday afternoon (3pm UK).

“Playing at home is always special and I’m super happy with how this week is going for me,” Jodar told Sky Sports. “It will be a great match. It will be my first time playing against Jannik so I hope I can give me best level.”

Jodar is the third Spanish teenager to reach the Madrid quarter-finals, following Rafael Nadal’s 2005 run and Alcaraz twice reaching the last-eight as a teenager in 2022 and 2023.

Jodar secured his first top-10 win by beating Alex de Minaur 6-3 6-1 in the second round on Friday, then backed that up with a 7-6 4-6 6-1 win over fellow 19-year-old Joao Fonseca.

open image in gallery Sinner was spotted watching Jodar earlier in the tournament ( Reuters )

Sinner was seen taking a court-side seat for Jodar’s win over De Minaur, the fifth seed, with the world No 1 absorbing the atmosphere as the Spaniard played in front of his home crowd.

"It's not gonna be the only time we face each other,” Sinner said of Jodar after his win over Norrie. “That's my feeling. It would be good if I face him before bigger tournaments coming up, Rome and Roland Garros.

“These are unique conditions here, he is from Madrid so he is used to the conditions. But at the same time I can have good feedback for bigger tournaments coming up. It’s very exciting. He’s a big, big talent.”

News.title: When UK’s social media plans for under-16s will be revealed
News.content:
The UK Government intends to put forward proposals to restrict social media for under-16s before the summer, with plans to legislate by the end of the year.

Technology Secretary Liz Kendall stated that the ongoing consultation explores various measures, including age restrictions, curfews, and limits on features like 'doom-scrolling'.

Esther Ghey, mother of murdered teenager Brianna Ghey, urged MPs to learn from Australia's social media ban for children and implement a more effective system in the UK.

Education Secretary Bridget Phillipson confirmed the Government's commitment to addressing addictive features on social media, aiming for robust and long-lasting solutions.

The Government's decision to introduce restrictions follows significant pressure from the House of Lords, led by Lord Nash, who described it as a “huge step forward” for children's online safety.

News.title: Shigella Infection
News.content:
Key facts

Shigella are bacteria that cause diarrhoea

Shigella infection, also called shigellosis, is very contagious.

It spreads easily through contaminated food, water, surfaces or objects, and from person to person.

The infection can also be spread through sexual activity

Infection is usually treated with fluids and rest, but sometimes antibiotics are necessary

Some strains of bacteria have become resistant to the drugs used to treat them.

Overview

Shigella bacteria cause an infection of the bowel known as shigellosis, which results in diarrhoea. There are four main species: Shigella sonnei, Shigella flexneri, Shigella boydii, and Shigella dysenteriae. Shigella is a major cause of moderate to severe diarrhoea globally, with an estimated 80-165 million cases each year, mostly in low or middle-income countries. It is estimated that there are around 200,000 deaths due to shigella infection every year, with 60,000 of these occurring in children under the age of five.

Shigellosis is highly contagious; it only takes a small number of bacteria to cause infection. People can continue to spread the bacteria for several weeks after they have recovered.

Signs and symptoms

Symptoms usually appear one to two days after infection and last for about seven days. However, symptoms can sometimes take up to a week to develop.

Most people experience:

Diarrhoea, which may be bloody or prolonged

Fever

Stomach pain

A feeling of needing to pass stool even when the bowels are empty Other possible symptoms may include:

Abdominal pain

Feeling sick

Vomiting

Dangers and complications

Shigella can be dangerous, particularly for children. The disease can cause severe bloody diarrhoea (dysentery), known as shigellosis, and can spread beyond the gut leading to blood poisoning, and in some cases sepsis and death. In places with poor sanitation and limited access to clean water, repeated infections can lead to stunted growth and impaired brain development.

Drug-resistant Shigella infections have increased significantly and a study in Nature Communications in 2023 showed that the number of cases of extensively drug resistant infections – meaning they cannot be treated with first and second line antibiotics – are growing, particularly among gay and bisexual men. In 2023 UK public health officials reported 97 cases compared to three the previous year.

Transmission

Shigella spreads easily because it is found in faeces, and swallowing just a small amount of the bacteria can cause illness. The bacteria can be transmitted through:

Contact with a sick person

Contaminated water or food

Contaminated surfaces or objects

Sexual activity

Flies that have landed on food

People who travel to areas with poor sanitation and unsafe water are more likely to get sick. Children under five years old are also at high risk of contracting the disease. Outbreaks often occur in schools and nurseries.

In recent years it has been recognised that shigella can also be transmitted through sexual activity as there have been outbreaks among men who have sex with men.

Treatment

Most people with shigellosis will recover without antibiotic treatment within five to seven days with rest and fluids. It is important to drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration. Antibiotics may be used against the most severe form of shigella, although the threat of antibiotic resistance means that these should be administered with caution.

Prevention

There is currently no vaccine against shigella, although nine are currently in development. However, there is unlikely to be any available until the 2030s. In the meantime the best way to avoid getting or spreading shigella is to follow these steps:

Wash hands with soap and water, especially after using the toilet, changing nappies and before preparing food

Be careful when changing nappies

Avoid swallowing water while swimming

Follow safe food and water habits and wash your hands often when travelling internationally

Avoid sexual contact for at least two weeks after diarrhoea ends, if you or your partner has been diagnosed with shigellosis

Use condoms, particularly if having sex with a new partner

Do not prepare or serve food for others until symptoms have stopped for 48 hours

Do not attend swimming pools, hot tubs or water parks until symptoms have stopped for 48 hours

History

Reports of dysentery date back to ancient times but in 1897 in Japan 20,000 people died from the disease in six months. During this outbreak, Dr Kiyoshi Shiga isolated and identified the bacteria responsible for the disease, which we now know as Shigella.

While antibiotics and improved sanitation have reduced the frequency of dysentery, Shigella still causes many deaths, particularly in lower-income countries. Scientists have been trying to develop vaccines against Shigella for over 100 years. There are currently nine vaccine candidates in clinical trials. A vaccine could reduce the reliance on antibiotics, therefore helping to reduce the growing problem of antimicrobial resistance.

While it is not classed as a sexually transmitted infection, since about 2012 the number of cases spread by men having sex with men has risen. The numbers grew after the pandemic with UK public health agencies reporting 230 cases in 2022 and 432 in 2023.

News.title: Severe Fever with Thrombocytopaenia Syndrome (SFTS)
News.content:
Key facts

Severe Fever with Thrombocytopaenia Syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging infectious disease caused by the SFTS virus (SFTSV)

It is a tick-borne infection but can also be transmitted from human to human in rare cases

The key features are high fever and a low platelet count (thrombocytopaenia).

Most infections occur in rural areas in parts of Asia

There is no specific treatment or vaccine

Overview

Severe fever with thrombocytopaenia syndrome (SFTS) first emerged in China in 2009 and is caused by the SFTS virus (SFTSV), also known as Huaiyangshan banyangvirus. SFTS is a tick-borne infection, but human-to-human transmission can also occur in rare cases, through direct contact with infected blood or bodily fluids. The illness often begins with flu-like symptoms and fever.

Most infections occur in rural areas where there is an increased presence of ticks. Human cases were first identified in Central and Eastern China and further cases have been identified in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. Additionally, SFTSV has been detected in stored blood samples from patients with thrombocytopaenia in Vietnam. There have also been reports of SFTS infection in Pakistan.

Researchers class it as a public health threat with pandemic potential as the carrier of the disease – the tick – has spread around the world.

Signs and symptoms

The key features of SFTS are high fever and a low platelet count. The illness often starts with flu-like symptoms and fever, which lasts for about seven days. The incubation period is usually between seven and 14 days, typically around nine days.

Other symptoms may include gastrointestinal problems such as abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhoea.

Some patients may experience only a mild illness, which resolves spontaneously.

Dangers and complications

In cases of progressive disease, severe illness typically develops in the second week. Reported complications include:

Acute kidney injury

Myocarditis

Haemorrhage

Meningoencephalitis

Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (a rare condition where white blood cells attack other blood cells)

Multi-organ dysfunction

In those who survive severe illness, signs of recovery usually emerge around days eight to 11 of illness, accompanied by a decrease in blood viral load and recovery of the platelet count. Case fatality rates have varied between 5.2 per cent in China to 32.6 per cent in South Korea.

Transmission

The disease is contracted via the bite of an infected tick, usually the Asian long-horned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis, but other types of tick can also transmit. Sheep, goat and other kinds of mammal are also carriers.

The disease can be passed from human to human via close contact – but precisely how this occurs is unclear. Spread of the infection has also been reported in A&E and intensive care departments.

Treatment

There is no proven, specific treatment for SFTS, and there is no vaccine. Treatment is focused on relieving symptoms. Any patient with SFTS in the UK would be treated in a high level critical care unit. The antiviral ribavirin has been administered but it is unclear how effective it is.

Prevention

Travellers who are hiking or doing other outdoor activities in endemic areas may be at increased risk and if travelling in areas where the disease has been reported to avoid tick bites. You should stay out of long grass and apply insect repellent, including on clothing and any equipment such as camping gear.

SFTS cases have occurred in Central and Eastern China, Western Japan, and rural areas of the Republic of Korea.

History

SFTS first emerged in China in 2009 and rapidly spread around the country. Since then cases have been reported in Japan, Korea, Vietnam and Taiwan. From 2010 to 2019, a total of 13,824 SFTS cases (8,899 lab-confirmed and 4,925 probable cases) were reported in mainland China. This includes 713 deaths.

It is unclear how the disease emerged but it is likely to be due to increased contact between humans and wildlife; and/or via migratory birds, who carry the tick as a parasite.

Researchers class this emerging disease as having the potential for pandemic spread.

nature.com/sfts-virus

gov.uk/severe-fever-with-thrombocytopaenia-syndrome

News.title: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS)
News.content:
Key facts

SARS is a viral respiratory illness caused by the SARS-associated coronavirus

The illness was first reported in late February 2003 in China

The 2003 global outbreak spread to 29 countries, resulting in 8,096 cases and 774 deaths.

It is a respiratory virus that can spread through the air and via contaminated surfaces

There have been no reported cases of the disease since 2004

Overview

Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) is a viral respiratory disease caused by a SARS-associated coronavirus. Most people who contracted it were previously healthy people between the ages of 25 and around 70. The first cases were in China in November 2002 before the disease spread around the world.

The SARS outbreak was the first severe and readily transmissible new disease of the 21st century and demonstrated the world’s interconnectedness by travelling on international travel routes. The global outbreak was contained by July 2003.

Signs and symptoms

The incubation period for SARS was typically two to seven days, but could be as long as 10 days. The first symptom was generally a fever.

Other symptoms included:

Headache

Malaise

Muscle pain

Mild respiratory symptoms

Some patients reported diarrhoea during the early stages.

After three to seven days, a lower respiratory phase began with the onset of a dry, non-productive cough or shortness of breath.

Dangers and complications

In 10 to 20 per cent of cases, the respiratory illness was severe enough to require intubation and mechanical ventilation. The case fatality rate among people with a confirmed case of the disease was estimated to be around 9.6 per cent.

Transmission

SARS is an airborne virus that spreads through small droplets of saliva, similar to how the common cold and influenza spread. It can also spread indirectly via surfaces touched by someone infected with the virus. An investigation by the World Health Organization showed that it may also have spread via inadequate plumbing systems in apartment buildings. Virus droplets may have entered apartments via strong extractor fans.

Treatment

There is no cure or vaccine for SARS. Antivirals were not shown to be effective during the outbreak and treatment was supportive and based on the patient’s symptoms, for example the administration of oxygen and intravenous fluids.

Prevention

Controlling outbreaks relies on containment measures, including:

Rapid detection of cases through good surveillance networks and early warning systems.

Isolation of suspected or probable cases.

Tracing to identify the source of infection and contacts of those who are sick.

Quarantine of suspected contacts for 10 days.

Exit screening for outgoing passengers from areas with recent local transmission.

Disinfection of aircraft and cruise vessels using WHO guidelines.

Personal preventive measures include frequent hand washing with soap or alcohol-based disinfectants. Those with a high risk of contracting the disease, such as health care workers, should use personal protective equipment, including a mask, goggles, and an apron. Household contacts should also wear a mask whenever possible.

History

The first cases of what would become known as SARS first emerged in the wet markets of Guangdong in 2002 when it is thought to have spilled over to humans from civet cats. However, the World Health Organization was not alerted to this new disease until February 2003. WHO issued its first global alert in March when a patient was hospitalised in Vietnam. However, as late as April that year Chinese officials were still covering up the scale of the outbreak.

The outbreak spread to 30 countries, with Hong Kong and Canada among the hardest hit, but by July 2003 WHO said it had been mostly contained.

SARS was a harbinger of what was to come during the Covid-19 pandemic as it spread quickly via international travel routes and exposed a lack of protective equipment for health care workers. Similar containment measures such as isolation of patients, contact tracing and mask wearing were also deployed.

News.title: Seasonal Flu
News.content:
Key facts

There are around a billion cases of seasonal influenza annually, including 3-5 million cases of severe illness

It differs from pandemic flu in that it is caused by an already circulating flu virus, whereas pandemic flu is a new virus against which people have little or no immunity

It causes 290,000 to 650,000 deaths every year..

Flu is very infectious and can easily spread to other people, with people being more likely to give it to others in the first five days.

Overview

Seasonal influenza, or the flu, is a common respiratory illness caused by flu viruses. It’s widespread and most people recover without needing medical attention. However, it can be severe or even deadly in some cases. There are four different types of flu virus: A, B, C and D. A and B virus cause seasonal flu.

Flu A includes subtypes like A(H1N1) and A(H3N2), with A(H1N1) being the virus behind the 2009 swine flu pandemic

Signs and symptoms

Flu symptoms start suddenly and typically appear one to four days after infection. Most people recover within a week.

Common symptoms include:

High fever or chills

Aches and pains

Dry cough

Fatigue

Sore throat

Headache

Runny or stuffy nose

Some may experience stomach issues like vomiting or diarrhoea, especially children.

The cough can last for two weeks or longer, and not everyone with the flu will have a fever.

Dangers and complications

While most people recover, flu can be more serious in certain high risk groups and can lead to serious complications such as pneumonia and sepsis. It can also worsen the symptoms of people with chronic conditions.

Flu-related hospitalisations and deaths mostly affect high-risk groups:

People 65 and older

Pregnant individuals

Young children (especially under two)

Those with weakened immune systems

If you or your child shows severe symptoms, seek medical help immediately.

Transmission

Flu spreads easily through respiratory droplets when someone coughs or sneezes. It’s most contagious in the first five days. In cold climates, flu seasons peak in winter, but in warmer areas, it can spread year-round.

It can spread easily in crowded places such as schools and nursing homes

Treatment

Most people recover without special treatment. To ease symptoms:

Rest, stay warm, and drink plenty of fluids

Take paracetamol or ibuprofen to reduce fever and pain

Children may need specific dosages for comfort

Antibiotics don’t work for the flu, but antiviral medicines can help if started early, especially for high-risk individuals.

Prevention

The annual flu vaccine is given to certain high risk groups in the UK. While it is less effective in older people, it still reduces severity and complications.

Other prevention tips include:

Wash your hands often

Cover your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing

Stay home if you’re sick and avoid contact with others

Avoid touching your face

Flu vaccines are updated routinely with new vaccines developed that contain viruses that match those circulating.

History

For many years flu was thought to be a bacterial infection and it was not until the 1930s that the first flu virus was identified.

There have been flu outbreaks and pandemics for many years, with the most well known and deadly in recent times being the 1918 Spanish flu pandemic. It swept around the world as troops came home at the end of the First World War and is estimated to have caused between 50 and 100 million deaths.

It was caused by the influenza A(H1N1) virus and, unlike many flu outbreaks, mainly affected healthy, young people. There were alarming complications such as sufferers turning blue as their bodies were starved of oxygen. Other less serious symptoms included explosive nosebleeds.

More recently, the A(H1N1) virus caused the 2009 swine flu pandemic, which is estimated to have caused around 280,000 deaths.

Seasonal flu vaccines are updated each year based on which strains of the virus are circulating.

Sports.title: Former Soccer Saturday pundit leaves fans shocked as Sky Sports icon posts graphic image of leg after knee surgery
Sports.content:
RODNEY MARSH shocked fans with a graphic image of his leg after having knee surgery.

The former QPR and Manchester City forward is regularly in contact with football fans on social media but left them stunned with his latest update.





Marsh, 81, showed off his nastily bruised left leg as it was being rested on a coffee table, posting on X: “In other news: I had knee surgery last week”.

The ex-Sky Sports Soccer Saturday pundit – who was capped nine times by England during his playing days – confirmed it was a full knee replacement with red blotches visible all the way up the inside of his thigh.

He thanked followers for the “good wishes and humour” after many got in touch to send him messages.

The Grumpy Pundits host on American radio station SiriusXM was told by one: “Good grief. Hope you’re not in too much pain.”

Another replied: “Speedy recovery Rodney! You can make the World Cup squad yet!”

After footage of Xavi Simons being treated for his ACL injury by Spurs medics went viral earlier this week, a third joked: “Just got off the phone with my mate who works at Tottenham’s medical department.

“He suggests a couple of sprints and a few star jumps”.

Someone else commented: “I think it’s time to give up those motorbike stunts! Get well soon mate”.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Two others went on “Magic sponge, sorted. Suck it up!” and “Followed by a shark attack by the looks of it”.

Popular and no-nonsense analyst Marsh had been on Soccer Saturday for 11 years before being sacked in 2005.

Marsh made a quip about the 2004 Boxing Day tsunami which killed over 200,00 people.

He quickly apologised but got the axe from Sky Sports.



Marsh said: “I apologise unreservedly for any offence I caused by my thoughtless and inappropriate comment I made.

“My intention was to make a light-hearted football joke.”

And recently he has hit out at the show, slamming it for being boring.

Marsh said: “It was edgy in those days, pushing the envelope a bit.

“Now it’s all b******s, all conforming to what people want to hear. It’s become very bland in my view.”

Sports.title: Incredible moment selfless former EFL star helps drag runner over London Marathon finish line
Sports.content:
FORMER EFL footballer Lee Brown was captured on video helping a distressed runner get over the finish line during the London Marathon.

The runner appeared powerless to continue but, on the home straight, Brown and another unknown male made sure they got to the end.





The runner wasn’t the only one who felt the pain of running 26.2 miles around the nation’s capital.

Dozens of runners had to be helped over the finish line either by their fellow marathon goers or people staffing the event.

Still, an extremely commendable effort from Brown, especially given so many runners are normally more concerned with their time.

Brown, 35, spent the majority of his career in League One and League Two making nearly 500 league appearances.



He also won three caps for England C during his career.

He appeared to run the marathon for the Make-A-Wish foundation, a charity that helps terminally ill children realise their dreams.

The London Marathon was especially notable this year thanks to Sabastian Sawe running a world record time.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It was the first time in history a runner has recorded a marathon in under two hours as the Kenyan did it with 30 seconds to spare.



Team GB star Eilish McColgan also made headlines after falling short of her personal best by 26 seconds, but for good reason.

The four-time Olympian’s ‘foot exploded’ about halfway through the run leaving her shoe a bloody mess.

Even with blood flooding her shoe and being unable to run properly, the Scot still managed to finish the race.

Sports.title: Truth behind Alisha Lehmann & Douglas Luiz’s split after ‘world’s sexiest’ footballer’s raunchy shoots & brutal put-down
Sports.content:
THEY were once football’s golden couple, but “the world’s sexiest footballer”, Alisha Lehmann and Premier League star Douglas Luiz are now locked in a messy and bitter public spat.

The glamorous pair made history with a romantic “couple transfer” to Italian giants Juventus last year, but the fairytale quickly morphed into a nightmare. Now, the exes are desperately trying to one-up each other with a series of PDA-packed snaps alongside their new lovers – and jaw-dropping alleged social media digs.



Swiss bombshell Alisha, 27, has moved on with former Love Island hunk Montel McKenzie, 28, while Brazilian ace Douglas, 27, is flaunting his new romance with 19-year-old Brazilian model Duda Gaspar.

But behind the loved-up selfies, insiders reveal a spectacular war of words is bubbling over.

The feud reached boiling point recently when fans spotted alleged explosive comments traded between the bitter exes on Instagram.



When Montel posted a cosy picture with his new girlfriend Alisha, Douglas allegedly couldn’t resist marking his territory, commenting: “I had it like that for a long time, bro.”

But Alisha wasn’t about to take the bait lying down. In a devastating alleged clapback posted to her Instagram stories, the blonde beauty hit where it hurts, writing: “Move on, handsome, you had a tiny one. My current boyfriend almost took my breath away hahaha.”

Understandably, the Insta story – which disappears after 24 hours – was screenshotted and shared widely.

While some fans have speculated the shocking screenshots could be the work of internet pranksters, the drama perfectly highlights the simmering tension between the former lovers following their disastrous split.

According to insiders, the couple’s on-off romance was doomed from the start, plagued by jealousy over Alisha’s skyrocketing fame and her refusal to tone down her sexy image.



The pair originally split in late 2022 after furious rows over Alisha releasing a raunchy calendar. Although they reconciled to make their historic joint move to Italy, the cracks quickly reappeared.

A source said: “Social media was always a big part of Alisha and Douglas’ relationship. Alisha knew she could grow her profile by posting pictures of her and Douglas all loved-up together over the years.

“However, her increased fame coincided with cracks appearing in their relationship.

“He was furious about her releasing her own calendar, and she had had enough of their arguments. Douglas is quite reserved, whereas Alisha loves to boost her profile.

“Douglas desperately wanted Alisha by his side in Italy, but in the end it just didn’t work out.”



It wasn’t long before their Italian dreams soon turned into a complete disaster.

The source added: “It was tough for Douglas in Turin. He struggled with injuries. While Alisha made a fantastic start on the pitch, scoring twice in her first 11 appearances for the women’s side, it wasn’t a huge surprise when they finally called full-time on their relationship.

“There was always an element of jealousy between the two of them, and they are still trying to get one up on each other even now.”



‘So loved up’

Now back in the UK playing for Leicester City, Alisha has taken her sizzling image to the next level by launching a Fanvue account, a subscription service similar to OnlyFans.

At the time of writing, bisexual Alisha – who previously had a relationship with her Switzerland teammate Ramona Bachmann, 35 – is charging fans a discounted rate of just under £3 per month to access her exclusive images, but supporters must fork out up to £22 to access some of her raunchier collections, including a seven-picture photo set simply captioned: “Shower time”.

“If Douglas didn’t like the thought of Alisha doing a calendar, he would’ve certainly disapproved of her selling sexy pictures online,” the source adds. “But Montel goes along with it.”

Unlike prudish Douglas, former Love Island star Montel – who was coupled up with Leah Taylor on the show – is no stranger to the limelight and is more than happy to play the fame game alongside his superstar girlfriend.

The smitten pair have been packing on the PDA, treating Alisha’s 15.6 million Instagram followers to videos of them smooching, cuddling, and frolicking together. In one cheeky video, Alisha is seen jumping into Montel’s arms, captioning it: “Train together, Stay together.”



Our source spills: “Montel and Alisha are so loved up. They can barely keep their hands off one another in private, and she loves to let the world see that in public, too. After being in Love Island, Montel is well aware that Alisha needs to put herself out there to boost her profile even further, and he’s more than happy to let her do so.”

Not to be outdone, Aston Villa midfielder Douglas has been loudly broadcasting his own new romance with teenage model Duda – the daughter of Arsenal legend and Nottingham Forest global head of football, Edu Gaspar.

The new couple recently made a very public display of affection during a trip to London, sharing a very visible smooch on Oxford Street before hitting the LEGO store.

Douglas plastered the snaps across Instagram, prompting Duda to gush in the comments: “I love living my life by your side, I love you baby.”

Duda has also been spotted playing the ultimate WAG, cheering on Douglas from the stands at Villa Park, wearing a replica shirt bearing his name.



“It’s still early days for Douglas and Duda, but she is a huge support to him,” the insider adds.

“With Alisha, she wasn’t able to go to a lot of his games because of her own career, but Douglas loves looking up and seeing Duda in the crowd. Ironically, Duda’s influencer career is just getting started, and she would love to have a multi-million follower account like Alisha’s.”

With both stars now back in the UK and parading their new high-profile romances, this messy football breakup shows absolutely no signs of reaching full-time.

Alisha Lehmann‘s representatives were contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Damning stats reveal Blues flops DID stop trying for Rosenior, academy stars’ fears & Estevao update
Sports.content:
CHELSEA looked miles better against Leeds than they did against Brighton.

And the statistics, overall, back up the impression of a team trying harder for interim head coach Calum McFarlane than they were for Liam Rosenior.





Unfortunately, the running numbers for the FA Cup semi-final are not yet publicly available.

So we do not know if Chelsea did better than on the Tuesday night, when Brighton ran 120.93km to the Blues’ 113.32km.

But other figures do show an improvement, starting with matchwinner Enzo Fernandez.

At the Amex the Chelsea skipper managed just one tackle, zero interceptions and delivered a lone key pass while also failing to muster a shot. There was not even a foul in anger.

Five days and one manager later there was his goal, one of two efforts on target, three key passes, three tackles and three fouls, all combining to a man of the match award for a captain’s performance.

McFarlane was unsparing in his praise of Fernandez, saying that his greatest quality was to deliver when things got tough.

Rosenor is unlikely to agree.

Under Enzo Maresca, Fernandez was one of Chelsea’s brightest players across the first half of the season, but the fight vanished in the late run under Rosenior – with the Blues losing seven of his last eight games.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Put his performances against Brighton, the game which got Rosenior the boot, and Leeds up against one another and it shows a player who can fight when he wants to, not – as McFarlane claimed – whenever the pressure is on.

But Fernandez was far from alone in upping his game against Leeds.

After the 3-0 Amex humiliation, soon-to-be-ex-boss Rosenior bemoaned how his team simply did not win duels or headers.

Surprisingly, the Blues actually won a higher percentage of their total battles against the Seagulls – 50.62 per cent compared to 50.41 per cent against Leeds.

But the fact is they contested the ball much more often in the FA Cup semi final, with 121 total duels compared to 81 against Brighton.



And thanks mainly to Tosin Adarabioyo, who won seven of his eight aerial duels against Leeds, Chelsea were better in the air, with a 48.87 win percentage compared to 42.31 against Brighton.

The number of high turnovers and high turnovers ending in shots – which included Enzo Fernandez’s winning goal – were up from Tuesday night.

But maybe the most telling stats relate to the Blues’ pressing.



They managed 13 pressing sequences against Leeds, after only five against Brighton.

Then there are the Passes Per Defensive Action (PPDA) figures. But, please, don’t be scared.

PPDA is a way of measuring the intensity of a team’s pressing. It records the number of passes the opposing team makes before the defending team tries to do something to stop them – a tackle, interception, foul.

On average, Brighton made 22.1 passes for every time Chelsea tried to get the ball off them. Leeds managed 10.4.

Of course, the difference is partly explained by the different styles of play adopted by Brighton and Leeds, with Daniel Farke’s team playing a much more direct game.



And Fabian Hurzeler’s Seagulls gave a much better performance than limp Leeds.

But that was mainly because they were allowed to by Chelsea.

Rob Green, the former England goalkeeper who spent the final year of his career at Chelsea, laid bare the concerns the club should have because of the contrast in effort levels between Tuesday night and Sunday afternoon.

Green was part of a squad which included leaders and stars such as Cesar Azpilicueta, Gary Cahill, N’Golo Kante, Eden Hazard, Olivier Giroud and Antonio Rudiger.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, he said: “They’re a product of the system they are in and in modern-day football.



“It’s ugly but they have all the power and it was epitomised by Fernandez, he ran the game, it was down to him how they played.

“That is not healthy for a football club but for Chelsea it gets them to finals. Give a player an inch, they take a mile.”

QUALITY PROGRAMM-ING

FAIR play to the FA and their printers for a quick turnaround on the semi-final programme.

Liam Rosenior’s sacking was officially announced at 5.20pm on Wednesday, less than 96 hours before kick-off against Leeds at Wembley.

Rosenior, like Leeds counterpart Daniel Farke, wrote some notes to go in the Blues’ section of the 68-page souvenir, with almost 25,000 copies due to be ready for sale.



Rosenior’s words were replaced at the last minute by a photograph of interim boss Calum McFarlane and some Chelsea players and staff after the 1-1 draw at Manchester City in January, the first game of his first temporary spell in charge.

The only error was giving McFarlane’s age as 40 – which was forgivable, since pretty much every media outlet had said the same.

In fact, the former Under-21 team boss is 38.



ANSWERING THE COL

LEVI COLWILL made his long-awaited return from injury over the weekend.

The England defender played the full 99 minutes as ten-man Chelsea beat Middlesbrough 1-0.

Colwill has been absent since day one of pre-season after suffering an ACL injury in training following just a two-week break after last summer‘s Club World Cup.

The 23-year-old required surgery on his knee and has been back training at Cobham for a number of weeks as the club carefully manage his return.

With that it mind, while Colwill made a successful return to competitive football on Saturday, it is deemed highly unlikely that he is risked in the first team matchday squad against Nottingham Forest on Monday.



While the possibility has not been completely ruled out, there is an expectation Chelsea will continue to take their time – even though Colwill still has hopes of playing again before the end of the season.

MAD TIMING

IT may be crunch time at the end of the season, but the Chelsea players have been given a mini-break thanks to the Premier League schedule.

After a relentless run since the turn of the year, with sacked boss Liam Rosenior hardly having a free mid-week during his doomed spell, the club have decided to allow the players some R&R.

Players will return to Cobham for training on Thursday ahead of Monday’s game against Nottingham Forest as they search for a first Premier League win since early March.

Enzo Fernandez, Joao Pedro and Marc Cucurella have hopped over to Madrid to take in some tennis.



Cobham remains open to players who want to continue working, with a number expected to be on site this week for individual work or recovery sessions.

SAMBA STEVE

ESTEVAO Willian’s World Cup dreams may not be over yet.

The Brazilian wonderkid suffered a grade four hamstring injury against Manchester United, which many assumed would rule him out of this summer’s tournament



But Estevao is not giving up hope.

A source close to the player told SunSport: “We hope his recovery will be fast.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We have little time, but his injury isn’t so complicated.”

Former Chelsea boss Carlo Ancelotti, now in charge of Brazil, would love to have Estevao as an option after already losing Real Madrid winger Rodrygo to injury.

Sports.title: Man City fuming over fixture hell that sees them play 3 times in 7 days in major Premier League title boost to Arsenal
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY have been left deeply frustrated at the Premier League after being handed a nightmare end to the season.

Pep Guardiola’s treble-chasing side will have to play three times in seven days during the final couple of weeks of the campaign.





And the Etihad giants have been left baffled at the way the Prem have thrown out all the proposals they put forward.

Their home game with Crystal Palace – originally scheduled for Carabao Cup final weekend – will now take place on Wednesday, May 13.

Three days later they will tackle Chelsea in the FA Cup final at Wembley.

And then on Tuesday, May 19 they will head back down south to play the game at Bournemouth which was due to be played two days earlier.



So as well as the hectic schedule, Guardiola has been handed a travel headache as they chase more silverware.

Title rivals Arsenal will now be hoping for a slip up from Pep’s men during their busy run-in.

The Prem knew they had to find a date for the Palace game as far back as February 4 – when City reached the Carabao Cup final.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

So there is a sense of dismay at the Etihad over why it has taken so long to schedule the game when alternative dates have been overlooked.



And they cannot understand why the principle of rescheduling games at the earliest possible moment has not been followed.

City sources say they put forward various alternatives in recent days but all were thrown out – partly due to opposition from other clubs.

Regarding the game against Palace, three different midweek options were offered – including last week.

Yet the Eagles were handed a Monday night television slot against West Ham – effectively ruling out the rest of the week.

City have learned that, had Liverpool beaten them in the FA Cup quarter final earlier this month, a proposal was in place for the Palace-West Ham game to be put back to Sunday May 19th.



Another suggestion was that City could have played Palace last week instead – while moving their trip to Burnley to the weeks when Oliver Glasner’s men are in Europa Conference League action.

The possibility of playing Bournemouth on May 12 and then Palace the following week was also discussed but not given the thumbs up.

City’s frustration is further increased by UEFA not wanting any Prem fixtures being played on Wednesday, May 20th, as the Europa League final will take place that night.

Current leaders Arsenal were allowed to play their rearranged game at Wolves in February despite the fact there were four Champions League knockout games that night.

The PL has referenced a principle that all FA Cup semi‑finalists should play in the first available midweek ahead of the semi‑final.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, City wanted the Bournemouth game on the 12th – which is in line with that principle, should it apply to the final – but it has been placed the week AFTER now.

The Etihad side also suggested the idea of playing at the Vitality on Thursday, May 21 but that has been thrown out as well.

Sports.title: Arsenal fans fume at Premier League as club forced into ‘disgraceful’ fixture change to comply with little-known rule
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans have been left furious over a change in the Premier League fixture schedule.

The Gunners were due to face Burnley on Sunday, May 17 in their final home game of the season.





However, that has now been moved to the following Monday.

The match will kick off at 8pm, making it harder for many fans to attend.

One supporter took to social media to write: “Absolute disgrace. Match-going fan gets screwed over once again. How many people’s plans are ruined as a result of this? Shame on this league.”

Another commented: “Absolute f*****g disgrace by the Premier League, no thought for fans whatsoever.”

A third said: “Disgusting and outrageous. Absolutely no thoughts for the fans again.”

While a fourth wrote: “Last game of the season on a Monday night. Horrendous.”

The Arsenal Supporters’ Trust has also released a statement on the change, suggesting that more needs to be done by the Prem to support matchgoing fans.

It read: “The Arsenal Supporters’ Trust is disappointed by the proposed 8:00pm Monday kick-off for Arsenal vs Burnley.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“This timing creates clear difficulties for both sets of supporters, particularly those travelling or relying on public transport, and increases costs and disruption.

“As the final home game of the season, it also means the traditional lap of appreciation will not take place until around 10:00pm, making it less accessible for many fans.

“We did engage with Arsenal ahead of the most recent broadcast deal, recognising that clubs, including Arsenal, play a role in approving these agreements and asking that it give greater weight to the impact on supporters of games being moved.

“While we understand the significant financial benefits involved and how they support the club’s growth, we would urge both Arsenal and the Premier League to do more so that scheduling better reflects the needs of match-going supporters.”

Each club must play at least one Premier League match on a Monday or a Friday night each season.



Arsenal are the only club yet to play on either day, which is why the fixture has been moved.

Meanwhile, title rivals Manchester City will have to play three times in six days during the final weeks of the campaign.

Their home game with Crystal Palace – originally scheduled for Carabao Cup final weekend – will now take place on Wednesday, May 13.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend, 40, lands World Cup job weeks after coming out of retirement to sign for English club
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED legend Antonio Valencia has landed a TV punditry job ahead of the World Cup.

The former right-back, 40, has linked up with TV broadcaster Telemundo Deportes and will be on its expert panel for this summer’s tournament.





He joins a line-up of high profile ex-players including Real Madrid legend Guti and Mexico icon Andres Guardardo.

Valencia announced the news on social media alongside a picture of him holding a mic in the Telemundo Sports studio.

He wrote on X: “I want to thank God for this new stage, and @TelemundoSports for the trust; I’ll try to give my best. See you at the World Cup 2026.”

Telemundo added: “The Legends team is taking shape! A lot of history and talent in Telemundo’s first expert reveal for the World Cup.

“Who do you think will complete the team? Enjoy the 2026 FIFA World Cup starting June 11 on Telemundo and Peacock TV.”

Valencia was popular figure during his time at Old Trafford, where he spent a decade between 2009 and 2019.

He played 339 times for the Red Devils as he scored 25 goals.

The former Ecuador star also won two Premier League titles, two League Cups, one FA Cup and the Europa League.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

After leaving United on a free transfer, he went back to his homeland with Ecuadorian side LDU Quito.

He then rounded off his career in Mexico with Queretaro for one season before retiring in 2021.

Valencia finished with a total of 577 total career outings, scoring 46 times.

He also managed 99 caps for Ecuador. He captained both United and the national team.



But he recently came out of retirement to play games for amateur side Wythenshawe, who play in the seventh tier of English football.

Wythenshawe have a star-studded veterans team featuring some big name players who once played in the top flight.

It has featured ex-Man City stars Stephen Ireland, Joleon Lescott and Nedum Onuoha, former Burnley man George Boyd, plus ex-Newcastle forward Papiss Cisse and Chelsea flop Danny Drinkwater.

Ireland announced Valencia’s signing as he posted a picture with the ex-defender on social media.

He wrote: “Never thought I’d say this but welcome to Wythenshawe @antoniovalencia2525. Big signing @wythyvetsfc.”

Sports.content:
Premier League season ticket list in full: How do Arsenal, Man Utd and Liverpool compare?

Clubs have taken different approaches to Premier League season ticket prices ahead of 2026/27 as some opt for a freeze and others increase the cost

View 3 Images How do Premier League season ticket prices compare?

Manchester City are the latest club to announce a freeze on season ticket prices for the 2026/27 campaign. But how does their cost compare to the rest of the top flight?

‌



The current Premier League season is drawing to a close, as Pep Guardiola's City battle Arsenal for the crown, the chase for Champions League qualification is as close as it gets and some big name sides are bidding to avoid the drop in Tottenham and West Ham.

‌



It is the Hammers who currently offer the cheapest adult season ticket, but rather unexpectedly, City hold the second-cheapest. This will continue into next season as well, after the club received widespread praise for announcing last week that all matchday prices would be frozen. The decision was rubber-stamped following discussions with the fan board City Matters on Thursday.

‌



Mirror Football looks at how this compares with other Premier League clubs, as rivals Manchester United have upped their prices by five per cent in some areas.

While United's most affordable adult season ticket for all 19 home Premier League fixtures next season will be priced at £646, City's will cost supporters just £425.

‌



View 3 Images United's prices have increased in some areas (Image: Getty)

Only West Ham, whose top-flight survival remains uncertain, are offering a more affordable season ticket at £345. That figure also only reflects their 2025/26 pricing, which remains subject to change for the following campaign.

United sit eighth on the current list, which incorporates the 2025/26 prices for clubs such as the Hammers, who are yet to reveal their ticket costs ahead of 2026/27.

Arsenal lead the way, with next season's cheapest adult season ticket priced at £967. The top three are all London clubs, with Chelsea in second place (£880) and Tottenham third (£856).

Spurs have kept their prices frozen for 2026/27, while Chelsea are yet to confirm their costs following the end of a lengthy price freeze last year. Liverpool are amongst the clubs to have raised season ticket prices, with their cheapest now available at £734, representing a rise of approximately three per cent.

‌



View 3 Images Liverpool fans have protested about price rises (Image: Getty)

Merseyside rivals Everton have taken a comparable approach, with the cheapest ticket at their new Hill Dickinson Stadium set at £640, a five per cent increase.

As for the steepest price hike, Sunderland supporters face a broadly 12 per cent rise on their season tickets following a successful campaign in the Premier League. Both the relegated Burnley and Wolves have been excluded.

Sports.title: John Stones won't get a statue - but he's been pure gold for Man City and Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
John Stones won't get a statue - but he's been pure gold for Man City and Pep Guardiola

John Stones will end ten years at Manchester City this summer, and whilst he may not get the plaudits of his great team-mates, he's been integral to Pep Guardiola's trophyladen period

View 2 Images John Stones will leave Man City have won the Premier League six times - and also been part of their treble success

John Stones might not get cast in bronze outside the Etihad, like some of his more celebrated team-mates have been - but for long periods of his illustrious decade-long spell with Manchester City, Stones was pure gold.

‌



He arrived at the Etihad from Everton in the summer of 2016, at the same time as Pep Guardiola. In the previous months, Guardiola had been instrumental in the signing of Stones, even though he hadn't officially taken charge. He wanted Stones for a reason.

‌



Because he rated him as the best footballing centre half in English football. And over the next 10 years, Stones proved Guardiola right.

‌



Despite suffering some cruel luck with injuries, Stones stood shoulder to shoulder with Guardiola in the process of turning City into the greatest club side of a generation. Perhaps the best one of all time in English football.

Stones has won 16 trophies, and was part of the side which claimed a historic Treble back in 2023. He cried on the pitch in Istanbul when attempting to sum up the achievement.

Man City plea to fall on deaf ears as Premier League stick to guns on fixture change READ MORE :

Man City announce John Stones exit as second Treble winner departs READ MORE :

Guardiola once said: "Since I arrived, he arrived. The many good things and the sad things, we lived together. We share it. He's an incredible human being."

‌



There was a reason he earned the nickname the Barnsley Beckenbauer. Because he is as comfortable on the ball as the German legend used to be. So much so that in that Treble winning campaign, Guardiola deployed Stones in a hybrid midfield role, which saw him operate in front of the back four alongside Rodri. Not a role your average defender would be trusted with.

View 2 Images ISTANBUL, TURKEY - JUNE 10: John Stones of Manchester City during the UEFA Champions League 2022/23 final match between FC Internazionale and Manchester City FC at Ataturk Olympic Stadium on June 10, 2023 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

At the peak of his powers, Stones was a classy combination of composure, speed, vision and calmness under pressure.

‌



"You don't quite appreciate him until tore playing alongside him," said Kyle Walker, who shared countless moments with Stones for both club and country. He rarely gets beat, is great on the ball and very calm and level headed."

Stones, who also appeared in two Euros finals with England and a World Cup semi final, will leave City in June. His contract has run down. And due to long standing fitness issues, has not been handed an extension.

It's an understandable decision, given City need to keep evolving. While Stones will also turn 32 next month. His best times are now behind him. But how good they were. And should never be forgotten.

Sports.title: Tottenham plot Marcus Rashford move as Barcelona make permanent transfer decision
Sports.content:
Tottenham plot Marcus Rashford move as Barcelona make permanent transfer decision

Marcus Rashford's future is the subject of much speculation after it emerged that Barcelona are unwilling to pay the £26million to make his move from Manchester United become permanent

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford's future remains unclear (Image: Alvaro Medranda/Getty Images)

Tottenham are reportedly interested in signing Marcus Rashford this summer if the Manchester United loanee doesn't end up joining Barcelona permanently. Rashford's loan spell at Barca concludes at the end of the 2025/26 season and there is uncertainty now surrounding his future.

‌



Rashford has made no secret of his desire to join Barcelona on a permanent deal this summer, having enjoyed this season. He has contributed 13 goals and 13 assists in 45 appearances for Hansi Flick's side and has no intention of returning to United.

‌



However, despite his impressive performances, Barca are dragging their heels in negotiations with United. They are unwilling to pay the £26million fee that would turn his loan into a permanent transfer and are keen to agree a fresh loan deal for the 2026/27 season, due to their much-publicised financial problems.

‌



United want a permanent transfer for their academy graduate, who still has two years left to run on a deal worth £325,000-a-week. They are standing firm on their stance with Barca - and the current stalemate could open the door for other interested parties.

FOLLOW OUR BARCELONA FB PAGE! Latest news and more from Camp Nou on our dedicated Facebook page

Julian Alvarez to Arsenal transfer bombshell dropped by Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone READ MORE :

Catalan outlet Sport says that Tottenham have shown 'genuine interest' in signing Rashford and could throw a spanner in the works, if they avoid relegation from the Premier League. Spurs currently sit 18th, two points from safety, with four matches left to play.

‌



Barcelona are prioritising a move for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez this summer and know the Argentina star will command a huge fee. They are therefore wary about over-spending on Rashford, who is not deemed to be a potential replacement for outgoing veteran centre-forward Robert Lewandowski.

Atleti manager Diego Simeone confirmed on Tuesday that Barca are among those chasing Alvarez. "It's normal that an extraordinary player like Julian Alvarez is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona," he said. "It's normal because he's very good."

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford's future could be tied to Julian Alvarez's this summer (Image: Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

‌



All of this muddies the waters for Rashford, who is understood to be staying calm as he tries to secure a dream move to Barcelona, where he has settled well and is enjoying life. The 28-year-old has a good relationship with Flick and is hopeful that the German manager's influence will be a significant factor.

United are set for a hugely significant summer transfer window, with the club hiring a new long-term manager to succeed Ruben Amorim while overhauling their squad. They want to fund the signing of an elite central midfielder through player sales, with Rashford on the transfer list alongside fellow loanees Rasmus Hojlund, Jadon Sancho and Andre Onana.

It is therefore in United's interests to secure a deal for Rashford as soon as possible, but Barca sporting director Deco is likely to try and negotiate a lower fee if a loan is off the table.
